strategy.thesis: Public-interest foundation established in April 2021 by the family of the late Hanmi Pharmaceutical Group founder Lim Sung-ki, using cash, real estate, and Hanmi Science shares donated by the family. It funds translational research into rare and intractable diseases -- from disease-mechanism elucidation and novel-target/candidate discovery through clinical-stage work -- and prizes outstanding biotech/pharma researchers, functioning as venture-philanthropy for Korea's rare-disease drug pipeline rather than making direct equity investments in startups.

lifesci.science_platform_notes: Runs two grant programs: the '임성기연구자상' (Lim Sung-ki Researcher Award) recognizing biotech/pharma researchers, and the '희귀난치성질환 연구지원사업' (Rare & Intractable Disease Research Support Program), which funds individual projects at roughly KRW 200 million per year for up to 3 years, covering the full cycle from pathophysiology and target discovery to clinical-stage development.

track_record.portfolio_count: 14 researchers across 4 rare-disease research projects funded 2022-2025 (cumulative ~KRW 3.2B)

summary.en: A Seoul-headquartered public-interest foundation founded in 2021 by the family of Hanmi Pharmaceutical Group's late founder Lim Sung-ki, funding translational rare-disease drug research (from target discovery through clinical stage) and prizing outstanding biotech/pharma researchers -- a venture-philanthropy model supporting Korea's rare-disease drug pipeline.
summary.local: 한미약품그룹 창업주 고(故) 임성기 회장의 유족이 2021년 설립한 공익재단으로, 희귀난치성질환의 병리기전 규명부터 치료 후보물질 발굴, 임상 단계까지 전주기 연구를 지원하고 생명공학·의약학 분야 우수 연구자를 시상한다.

verification_notes: Grant-making research-philanthropy foundation, not a direct equity investor in companies; funded by Hanmi Pharm annual donations and dividends on Hanmi Science shares held by the Lim family (per theguru.co.kr). HQ presumed Seoul (Hanmi Group's home base) but not independently confirmed via a quoted source, so hq_city was left unset. Other South Korean organizations were investigated for this angel-network/family-office/venture-philanthropy slice and excluded as insufficiently verified or out of scope: (1) Korea Bio-Health Investment Consortium / 바이오헬스투자협의체 (investbio.or.kr) is an industry networking platform operating under the Korea Drug Research Association that connects companies, VCs, and accelerators and occasionally organizes co-investment vehicles -- it is not itself an angel network or family office and its membership is dominated by corporates/VCs/universities, not health-focused angels; (2) Nanum Angels / 나눔엔젤스, though listed as an 'accelerator' member of the above consortium and reported to have made one healthcare seed deal, states on its own site that its focus is lifestyle-sector entrepreneurs (fashion, food, prop-tech), not health, so it lacks a dedicated medical nexus; (3) Korea Rare Disease Foundation / 한국희귀질환재단 (kfrd.org) is a patient-advocacy and support organization, not a research funder or investor; (4) Boars' Club, a family-office network cited in Korean press for supporting Korean startups, is headquartered in Los Angeles with no dedicated Korea fund or office, so it falls outside this region's scope per the entity-inclusion rule.
